original_question: If G is a graph of order n, must the third and fourth largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_i(G) <= floor(n/i) for i = 3 and i = 4?
target_in_paper: Section 19.1, Problem 10 (Powers [139]) in "The third and fourth eigenvalues of graphs": the question whether Powers's bound λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋ holds for i = 3 and i = 4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target very closely: it is about an n-vertex graph G, the third and fourth largest adjacency eigenvalues, and the specific bound λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋ for i = 3, 4. That matches the official statement of Problem 10 essentially verbatim once the paper's notation is unpacked.
missing_details: The paper's global convention is that graphs are simple, undirected, and unweighted; your draft just says "graph."
The notation λ_i(G) should be defined explicitly as the i-th largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G), with ordering λ_1(G) ≥ λ_2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λ_n(G).
The parameter n should be identified as the order of G, i.e. n = |V(G)|.
The quantifier should be made explicit: the question asks whether the inequality holds for every graph G of order n, for each i in {3,4}.

To stay paper-faithful, it helps to note that this appears in Section 19.1 as Powers's proposed extension of his more general bound λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋, which the survey says is clear for i ≤ 2 and false for i ≥ 5.
The nearby context also records that the survey itself mentions a counterexample for i = 4 due to Linz; your draft does not indicate that caveat.
refined_question: Let G be a simple undirected unweighted graph with n = |V(G)|, and let λ_1(G) ≥ λ_2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λ_n(G) be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix A(G). Is it true that λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋ for each i ∈ {3,4}?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact target, namely Problem 10 in Section 19.1. I kept the question narrowly focused on the same inequality and the same indices i = 3,4, and only added the paper's standing conventions and eigenvalue notation so that the question is fully self-contained. I did not replace it with Hong's broader Problem 11, because the paper presents that as a neighboring, more general problem rather than as an equivalent reformulation. The nearby context in the survey is that Powers had an upper bound λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋, that the bound is straightforward for i ≤ 2, fails for i ≥ 5, and that the survey also notes a counterexample for i = 4 by Linz.
